title: Do you read to show off
paragraphs: What do you read when you are travelling by train or bus? What are other passengers reading? Perhaps a woman sitting near you is reading a trashy romantic novel. A man is reading a serious biography about a politician. And there's a student reading an English textbook.

What do their choices say about them? Do you judge them by what they are reading? I have got to tell you that your impressions of them are probably completely wrong. The woman reading the romantic novel could be a lawyer. She just wants a light read to take her mind off work.
The man reading the biography wants you to think that he is an intellectual, but he is just showing off. The student reading the textbook isn't a student at all. She's an English teacher.

Publishers know that some people are self-conscious about what they read on public transport and so they put out different versions of a cover. For example, books about Harry Potter have an original cover for young readers and then another more serious version for adults.

So next time you are on a train, look around and see what other people are reading, but don't jump to any conclusions. You will probably be wrong. Here is a situation where you could say, "Don't judge a book by its cover".

vocabulary.term: trashy [ˈtræʃi] adj. 俗气的，低劣的
vocabulary.entry: trashy [ˈtræʃi] adj. 俗气的，低劣的
vocabulary.example: She picked up a trashy magazine to kill time on the bus.
vocabulary.translation: 她拿起一本俗气的杂志在公交车上打发时间。

vocabulary.term: romantic novel [rəʊˈmæntɪk ˈnɒvl] n. 言情小说
vocabulary.entry: romantic novel [rəʊˈmæntɪk ˈnɒvl] n. 言情小说
vocabulary.example: Her favorite genre of books is romantic novel.
vocabulary.translation: 她最喜欢的书籍类型是言情小说。

vocabulary.term: biography [baɪˈɒɡrəfi] n. 传记
vocabulary.entry: biography [baɪˈɒɡrəfi] n. 传记
vocabulary.example: He spent a month reading a biography of a famous writer.
vocabulary.translation: 他花了一个月时间读一本著名作家的传记。

vocabulary.term: politician [ˌpɒləˈtɪʃn] n. 政治家
vocabulary.entry: politician [ˌpɒləˈtɪʃn] n. 政治家
vocabulary.example: The biography focuses on the life of a respected politician.
vocabulary.translation: 这本传记聚焦于一位受尊敬的政治家的生平。

vocabulary.term: impression [ɪmˈpreʃn] n. 印象
vocabulary.entry: impression [ɪmˈpreʃn] n. 印象
vocabulary.example: Her calm attitude left a good impression on the interviewer.
vocabulary.translation: 她冷静的态度给面试官留下了好印象。

vocabulary.term: light read [laɪt riːd] n. 轻松读物
vocabulary.entry: light read [laɪt riːd] n. 轻松读物
vocabulary.example: A comic book is a perfect light read for a lazy afternoon.
vocabulary.translation: 漫画书是慵懒午后的绝佳轻松读物。

vocabulary.term: take one's mind off [teɪk wʌnz maɪnd ɒf] phr. 使不去想，转移注意力
vocabulary.entry: take one's mind off [teɪk wʌnz maɪnd ɒf] phr. 使不去想，转移注意力
vocabulary.example: Listening to music helps take my mind off work stress.
vocabulary.translation: 听音乐能帮我转移对工作压力的注意力。

vocabulary.term: intellectual [ˌɪntəˈlektʃuəl] n. 知识分子；adj. 智力的，知识型的
vocabulary.entry: intellectual [ˌɪntəˈlektʃuəl] n. 知识分子；adj. 智力的，知识型的
vocabulary.example: He pretends to be an intellectual by reading classic books in public.
vocabulary.translation: 他通过在公共场合读经典书籍假装自己是知识分子。

vocabulary.term: show off [ʃəʊ ɒf] phr. 炫耀，卖弄
vocabulary.entry: show off [ʃəʊ ɒf] phr. 炫耀，卖弄
vocabulary.example: The boy likes to show off his new toy to his classmates.
vocabulary.translation: 这个男孩喜欢向同学炫耀他的新玩具。

vocabulary.term: publisher [ˈpʌblɪʃə(r)] n. 出版商，出版人
vocabulary.entry: publisher [ˈpʌblɪʃə(r)] n. 出版商，出版人
vocabulary.example: The publisher decided to print more copies of the bestseller.
vocabulary.translation: 出版商决定多印刷这本畅销书的册数。

vocabulary.term: self-conscious [ˌself ˈkɒnʃəs] adj. 不自在的，难为情的
vocabulary.entry: self-conscious [ˌself ˈkɒnʃəs] adj. 不自在的，难为情的
vocabulary.example: She feels self-conscious speaking in front of a large group.
vocabulary.translation: 她在一大群人面前说话会感到不自在。

vocabulary.term: public transport [ˈpʌblɪk ˈtrænspɔːt] n. 公共交通工具
vocabulary.entry: public transport [ˈpʌblɪk ˈtrænspɔːt] n. 公共交通工具
vocabulary.example: Many people rely on public transport to go to work.
vocabulary.translation: 很多人依赖公共交通工具上班。

vocabulary.term: version [ˈvɜːʃn] n. 版本
vocabulary.entry: version [ˈvɜːʃn] n. 版本
vocabulary.example: The novel has a simplified version for young readers.
vocabulary.translation: 这本小说有面向青少年读者的简化版本。

vocabulary.term: cover [ˈkʌvə(r)] n. 封面
vocabulary.entry: cover [ˈkʌvə(r)] n. 封面
vocabulary.example: The book has a beautiful cover designed by a famous artist.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书的封面由著名艺术家设计，十分精美。

vocabulary.term: original [əˈrɪdʒənl] adj. 原始的，最初的
vocabulary.entry: original [əˈrɪdʒənl] adj. 原始的，最初的
vocabulary.example: The original cover of the book is more popular among children.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书的原始封面更受孩子们欢迎。

vocabulary.term: jump to conclusions [dʒʌmp tu kənˈkluːʒnz] phr. 急于下结论
vocabulary.entry: jump to conclusions [dʒʌmp tu kənˈkluːʒnz] phr. 急于下结论
vocabulary.example: Don't jump to conclusions before you know all the facts.
vocabulary.translation: 在了解所有事实之前别急于下结论。

vocabulary.term: genre [ˈʒɒnrə] n. （文学、艺术等的）类型，体裁
vocabulary.entry: genre [ˈʒɒnrə] n. （文学、艺术等的）类型，体裁
vocabulary.example: Science fiction is my favorite genre of movies and books.
vocabulary.translation: 科幻是我最喜欢的电影和书籍类型。

vocabulary.term: kill time [kɪl taɪm] phr. 打发时间
vocabulary.entry: kill time [kɪl taɪm] phr. 打发时间
vocabulary.example: He likes to play mobile games to kill time on the subway.
vocabulary.translation: 他喜欢在地铁上玩手机游戏打发时间。

vocabulary.term: focus on [ˈfəʊkəs ɒn] phr. 聚焦于，集中注意力在
vocabulary.entry: focus on [ˈfəʊkəs ɒn] phr. 聚焦于，集中注意力在
vocabulary.example: The report focuses on the problems of public transport.
vocabulary.translation: 这份报告聚焦于公共交通存在的问题。

vocabulary.term: rely on [rɪˈlaɪ ɒn] phr. 依赖，依靠
vocabulary.entry: rely on [rɪˈlaɪ ɒn] phr. 依赖，依靠
vocabulary.example: Older people often rely on their children for daily care.
vocabulary.translation: 老年人的日常照料往往依赖子女。

sentences.english: What do you read when you are travelling by train or bus?
sentences.chinese: 你坐火车或公交车时读什么？

sentences.english: Perhaps a woman sitting near you is reading a trashy romantic novel.
sentences.chinese: 也许坐在你旁边的一位女士正在读一本俗气的言情小说。

sentences.english: A man is reading a serious biography about a politician.
sentences.chinese: 一位男士正在读关于一个政治家的严肃传记。

sentences.english: And there's a student reading an English textbook.
sentences.chinese: 还有一个学生正在读英语课本。

sentences.english: What do their choices say about them?
sentences.chinese: 他们的选择说明了什么？

sentences.english: Do you judge them by what they are reading?
sentences.chinese: 你会根据他们读的内容来评判他们吗？

sentences.english: I have got to tell you that your impressions of them are probably completely wrong.
sentences.chinese: 我得告诉你，你对他们的印象可能完全错了。

sentences.english: The woman reading the romantic novel could be a lawyer.
sentences.chinese: 读浪漫小说的女士可能是一名律师。

sentences.english: She just wants a light read to take her mind off work.
sentences.chinese: 她只是想读点轻松的东西以便不去想工作的事情。

sentences.english: The man reading the biography wants you to think that he is an intellectual, but he is just showing off.
sentences.chinese: 读传记的男士想让你认为他是个知识分子，但他只是在炫耀。

sentences.english: The student reading the textbook isn't a student at all.
sentences.chinese: 读课本的学生根本不是学生。

sentences.english: Publishers know that some people are self-conscious about what they read on public transport and so they put out different versions of a cover.
sentences.chinese: 出版商知道有些人对在公共交通工具上读什么感到不自在，因此他们提供了不同版本的封面。

sentences.english: For example, books about Harry Potter have an original cover for young readers and then another more serious version for adults.
sentences.chinese: 例如，关于哈利·波特的书有面向年轻读者的原始封面，还有面向成年人的更严肃的版本。

sentences.english: So next time you are on a train, look around and see what other people are reading, but don't jump to any conclusions.
sentences.chinese: 所以下次你在火车上时，环顾四周看看其他人在读什么，但不要急于下结论。

sentences.english: Here is a situation where you could say, "Don't judge a book by its cover".
sentences.chinese: 这就是一个可以说“不要以貌取人”的情境。
